title: Phở and friends
intro: Eleven things to eat and drink in Hà Nội, and the word to praise them. Each syllable is coloured by its tone, so you see the tone as well as hear it.

foe.name: Mèo Béo
foe.intro: He has stolen your phở and he will not give it back.

taunts.vi: Meo meo! Phở này là của tôi!

win.vi: Thôi, trả phở cho bạn đây!
win.en: Fine, here is your phở back!

words.hook: Picture a friend tasting phở for the first time with a doubtful "fuh...", voice dropping, then finishing the whole bowl.
words.tip: ph sounds like f. The hỏi tone starts at your normal pitch and drops further and faster than huyền.

words.hook: Grandma calls "Come!" because the rice is ready.
words.tip: ơ is like the vowel in British "fur", with no r. Keep the tone level.

contrast.en: green rice flakes (a Hà Nội treat)

words.hook: A bundle of thin white noodles drops from the sky like a boon, and you shout "boon!" with your voice rising.
words.tip: u is the "oo" in "moon". The sắc tone rises.

words.hook: The crust is so crunchy it goes "bang!", and everyone at the table shouts "me!".
words.tip: In Hà Nội, anh sounds close to "ain" with a soft ng at the end. mì is "mee", falling low.

words.hook: A hen settles onto her nest with a long, low "gaaa", her voice sinking like the huyền tone.
words.tip: g is soft: the back of your tongue nearly touches where English k is made, but air keeps flowing, like the g in Spanish "lago". The huyền tone starts a little below your normal pitch and falls gently, slightly breathy.
words.note: g for game bird: gà is chicken. Do not mix it up with cá (fish).

words.hook: A beefy bull gives a long, low "baw", the aw of British "saw", sinking gently like the huyền tone.
words.tip: o is open, like the "aw" in British "saw". The huyền tone falls gently.
words.note: b for beef: bò is beef, and the cow it comes from.

words.hook: A fish leaps out of the river and you shout "ca!", your voice shooting up as you try to catch it.
words.tip: c is a k with no puff of air.
words.note: c for carp: cá is fish.

words.hook: A mountain of fresh herbs so big you say "zow!".
words.tip: In Hà Nội, r sounds like z, so rau sounds like "zow" (rhymes with "cow"), with a short, quick a.

words.hook: You jump into a cool lake on a hot day and come up with one quick, rising gasp: "noo-uhk!"
words.tip: ươ glides from ư (say "oo" with your lips spread) to ơ. The final c is cut short, not released.

words.hook: Tea is "chai" in many languages. After the first sip you sigh "chà", your voice falling.
words.tip: In Hà Nội, tr sounds like the ch in "chip", but with no puff of air.
words.note: Hà Nội also says chè for tea (nước chè, chè xanh).

words.hook: It is the French word café, said the Vietnamese way.
words.tip: ê is like the "ay" in "say", without the glide at the end.

words.hook: The food is so good you start singing: "sing-ngon... ngon!".
words.tip: ng is the sound at the end of "sing". Start the word with it.

contrast.en: tip, top (of a tree or flame)

grammar.title: The main word comes first
grammar.text: In Vietnamese the thing comes first and the word that describes it follows. phở bò is pho + beef: beef pho. Describing words follow the same rule: cá ngon is tasty fish. Said on its own, Cá ngon! also means "The fish is tasty!", because Vietnamese needs no word for "is" before a describing word.

combos.note: quá after a word means "so" or "really": ngon quá! Before a word it usually means "too": quá cay, too spicy. Hà Nội people also say Ngon thế!
